# Host note (11-17): the fleet print reader's reading of Brinon-Conrad and Berger's survey (copied verbatim in substance)

Source read: Brinon-Conrad, CMI notes, preliminary version dated June 24, 2009 (cited in the manuscript as
`brinon-conrad`; PDF page = printed page), and Berger's survey arXiv:math/0210184v1, on the page images.

- Brinon-Conrad fixes every definition at definition level, inside the manuscript's bibliography.
  * A_cris, p. 129: sums of a_n xi^n/n! with a_n in W(R) tending to 0 for the p-adic topology (p. 128: generated by
    divided powers of any generator of ker theta); matches `AcrisOf`, including the topology.
  * B_cris, Def. 9.1.4, p. 131: B_cris^+[1/t] = A_cris[1/t] inside B_dR; matches `BcrisOf`.
  * B_st, Def. 9.2.3, p. 138 (abstract), embedded in B_dR on p. 142 by X -> log([q]) = log_dR([q]/q) + log_K(q),
    canonical once log_K(p) in K_0 is fixed (p. 143); Thm 9.2.10, p. 143: K tensor_{K_0} B_st injects into B_dR.
    With q~ = p~ and log(p) = 0 the image is B_cris[log_dR([p~]/p)], which is `BstFOf`.
  * Admissible, section 5.2, pp. 67-68: the dimension form dim_E D_B(V) = dim_F V (Thm 5.2.1(1): equivalent to
    alpha_V being an isomorphism; "semi-stable" means B_st-admissible, p. 68).
  * Potentially semistable, Thm 9.3.5, p. 148, definition printed inside the statement (V is semistable as a
    G_K'-representation for some finite K'/K); matches `IsPstF` with K = Q_p.
- So "potentially semistable in the sense of Fontaine" is definition-level inside the bibliography; per the reader,
  PanPrintedF then needs only the model-independence lemma (task item (b)).
- Berger's survey: II.2.2 (p. 11) defines omega and proves on the page that it generates ker theta (matchable).
  II.3.1 (p. 13) does not name the topology on its ring; Brinon-Conrad p. 129 fixes it as p-adic (what the Lean uses).
  II.3.3 (pp. 14-15) has two misprints: the log series is printed with exponent n-1 where it must be n (the Lean's n is
  right and agrees with Brinon-Conrad p. 142), and Frobenius is printed as phi(Y) = Y^p where the standard is pY (no
  effect on the Lean, which has no Frobenius).
- Lead's additions (same commit as the in-place restatement): (1) re-cite the `BstFOf` docstring to Brinon-Conrad
  p. 142 and Thm 9.2.10 instead of the survey's misprinted II.3.3 series (optionally noting the misprints); (2) wherever
  a docstring means a definition (A_cris, B_cris, B_st, admissibility, potentially semistable), cite Brinon-Conrad at
  the locators above rather than the survey. Survey misprints go to the report's Known-issues section.
